about.body1: ShrinkIt is a free online tool for resizing, compressing and converting images. It was built around one simple idea: your photos should never have to leave your device just to become smaller.
about.body2: Every operation — decoding, resizing, format conversion and download — happens locally in your browser using modern web APIs. There is no account, no upload queue and no server storing your files, because there is no server involved at all.

info1.p1: Every digital photo is a grid of tiny coloured dots called pixels. Your camera or phone decides how many dots fit in each row and column — a 4000×3000 photo holds 12 million of them, which is where the word “megapixel” comes from.
info1.p2: Each dot has to be stored somewhere, so more dots means more bytes. The file format matters too: JPG squeezes similar colours together to save space, while PNG keeps every dot exactly as it is — which is why the same picture can weigh 200 KB in one format and 2 MB in another.
info1.p3: When a site talks about “file size”, it simply means this storage weight, usually shown in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB).
info1.title: What is an image file size?
info2.p1: There are two levers, and they do different things. Resizing changes the dot grid itself — shrinking a photo from 4000×3000 to 1900×1100 throws away roughly three quarters of the pixels, so the file gets dramatically smaller without looking any different at normal viewing sizes.
info2.p2: Compression keeps the grid but stores it more cleverly. With JPG you pick a quality level: 90% looks identical to the original for most photos, while 60% can halve the file size again with only tiny artefacts if you look very closely.
info2.p3: The practical recipe: first resize to the dimensions you actually need — about 1900×1100 is plenty for the web — then save as JPG at around 90% quality. That is exactly what this tool does in one click, and your images never leave your device while it happens.
info2.title: How can I reduce my image's file size?

privacy.intro: This page explains in plain language what happens to your images when you use ShrinkIt.
privacy.s1d: When you add an image, it is read into your browser's memory. Decoding, resizing, format conversion and the download are all performed locally on your device using standard web APIs (Canvas, Web Workers). At no point is your image transmitted to ShrinkIt or to any third party, because there is no server component to send it to.
privacy.s1t: 1. Your images never leave your device
privacy.s2d: ShrinkIt strips metadata (EXIF) from processed images by default, which removes things like camera model, GPS coordinates and timestamps. You can optionally keep the original metadata with the “Keep photo metadata (EXIF)” switch; even then, the data stays inside the file you download — it is never sent anywhere.
privacy.s3d: This site uses no analytics, no advertising trackers and no cookies for tracking. If you install ShrinkIt as an app, its offline cache also lives only on your device.
privacy.s4d: Because everything runs locally, closing the tab ends the story: there is no account to delete and no server copy to request. If you have questions about this policy, reach out via the contact page.
privacy.s4t: 4. Nothing to delete, because nothing is stored
privacy.s5d: The extension asks only for the permissions it needs: a right-click menu entry for images, temporary session storage for a right-clicked image until the Editor reads it once, and synced storage for your settings such as language and theme. It never reads your browsing history, and it never sends your images or settings anywhere.
privacy.s5t: 5. Extension permissions, kept to the minimum
privacy.s6d: If this policy ever changes, the updated text ships with the extension itself — there is no server copy to update separately. The version history in the extension listing shows what changed.
privacy.sec1.body: This Privacy Policy explains what happens to your information when you use ShrinkIt, the free image resizing and compression service at shrinkit.dusrel.com. Each section stands on its own, and the summary at the top gives the essential picture.
privacy.sec1.title: 1. How to read this policy, who operates ShrinkIt, and how to contact us
privacy.sec10.body: ShrinkIt is a general-purpose image tool, not directed at collecting information from children, and it collects information from no one, child or adult. There are no accounts, profiles, messaging, or feeds, and the service never asks for anyone's age.
privacy.sec10.title: 10. Children
privacy.sec11.body: The most important security fact is architectural: there is no server store of your images or personal information to be breached. Risks like a leaked database of uploaded images cannot arise, because no such database exists.
privacy.sec11.title: 11. Security: what the architecture does and does not protect against
privacy.sec12.body: Privacy laws in India, Europe, the United Kingdom, California, Brazil, and elsewhere give you rights over your personal information. Because ShrinkIt holds no server copy of your images or personal information, most requests are answered by explaining that there is nothing held to return or delete.
privacy.sec12.title: 12. Your rights: India, Europe, the United Kingdom, California, Brazil, and everywhere else
privacy.sec13.body: ShrinkIt does not send your images or personal information across borders at the application level, because the app sends nothing at all. Your images never leave your device, so they are never transferred to another country or server.
privacy.sec13.title: 13. International transfers
privacy.sec14.body: At the application level, nothing is retained, because nothing is collected. Your images are held in memory only while the page is open and released when it closes; your settings and outputs are never retained on a server.
privacy.sec14.title: 14. Retention: how long information is kept
privacy.sec15.body: This policy may change from time to time as features, infrastructure, or the law change. The new version will be published on this page, and the last-updated date at the top will show the date from which it applies.
privacy.sec15.title: 15. Changes to this policy
privacy.sec16.body: Questions about this policy, requests to exercise a right, or complaints about how your information has been handled: write to hello@shrinkit.dusrel.com. Describe clearly what you are asking for, and include enough detail to understand the matter.
privacy.sec16.title: 16. Contact and complaints
privacy.sec2.body: ShrinkIt is a client-side service: the program that does the work is delivered to your browser as part of the page, then runs on your own device. Your image is read into your browser's memory, transformed there, and offered back as a download — it is never uploaded.
privacy.sec2.title: 2. What ShrinkIt is: a client-side service that works on your device
privacy.sec3.body: Your image goes through a short journey that stays entirely inside your browser: you add it, it is decoded and transformed in memory, and you download the result. There is no step at which the image leaves your device.
privacy.sec3.title: 3. What happens to your images, step by step
privacy.sec4.body: The same journey applies to every feature — resizer, target-size tools, passport, social, and comparison — and in every case the answer to “does this feature send your image anywhere?” is no.
privacy.sec4.title: 4. What each feature does with your data
privacy.sec5.body: ShrinkIt does not collect, receive, store, or have access to your images, your account details (there are no accounts), your browsing activity, or any analytics about you, because there is no backend and no analytics.
privacy.sec5.title: 5. What ShrinkIt does not collect
privacy.sec6.body: Your browser keeps a small amount of local data: your theme choice, and the service worker's cache of the site's own files so it loads reliably. None of it is visible to ShrinkIt, and none of it contains your images.
privacy.sec6.title: 6. What stays on your device
privacy.sec7.body: The app itself sends nothing about your images anywhere. But the site is delivered over the web, so the hosting infrastructure necessarily sees ordinary request-level information — such as your IP address and browser details — as any web host does. The site's font is self-hosted, so no font provider is involved.
privacy.sec7.title: 7. What the hosting and font infrastructure necessarily sees
privacy.sec8.body: ShrinkIt does not set cookies in normal use: no cookies for analytics, advertising, tracking, or personalisation, and no login session, because there are no accounts. The language is carried in the page address, not in a cookie.
privacy.sec8.title: 8. Cookies and similar technologies
privacy.sec9.body: The only way to contact us is by email at hello@shrinkit.dusrel.com. There is no contact form, so nothing you type into a form is ever transmitted. Do not include anything sensitive in your email that you would not want handled over ordinary email.
privacy.sec9.title: 9. Contact by email: what happens when you write to us

settings.resolution_tip: Dots per inch — written into JPG/PNG metadata and used to convert cm/inches to pixels.
